The PKGBUILD is for the selenium-manager package from SeleniumHQ. When analyzed for the narrow safety gate of running makepkg --printsrcinfo, only the global/top-level scope code is relevant, since function bodies (prepare(), build(), package()) are not executed during this command.

The top-level scope consists entirely of standard variable definitions: simple scalar variables (pkgver, url, etc.), array definitions (arch, depends, makedepends, options), and the source and sha256sums arrays. There are no command substitutions (no $(...) or backticks), no eval, no network requests, and no execution of downloaded code at the top level. The source array merely records a URL (pointing to the official SeleniumHQ GitHub repository) without downloading or executing it. No exfiltration, obfuscation, or dangerous command is present in the global scope.

Code inside the functions (e.g., cargo fetch, cargo build, install) is standard for a Rust-based package build and will be audited separately in the full PKGBUILD review, but it does not execute during makepkg --printsrcinfo.

This PKGBUILD follows standard Arch packaging practices for a Rust/Python project. The source is fetched from the official SeleniumHQ GitHub repository (https://github.com/SeleniumHQ/selenium), which is the legitimate upstream. A specific sha256sum is provided rather than using SKIP, ensuring integrity verification. The build process uses standard `cargo fetch`, `cargo build --frozen --release`, and the package function installs the binary and creates a symlink in Python's site-packages — all routine operations. No suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, eval/base64 usage, or unexpected file operations are present. The Python site-packages path is computed dynamically via `import site`, which is standard Arch packaging convention.
